processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds could be moved stepwise inside the furnace and were successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition in the ingot was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled into 2±0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2×60×55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregation of Mn; single austenite phase at room temperature (Al content below 5 wt.%).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

comparative_performance.benchmark_alloy_id: alloy_fe-30mn-1.2c (0 wt.% Al) and alloy_fe-30mn-1.2c-8al (8 wt.% Al)
comparative_performance.comparison_metric: sensitivity of mechanical properties (YS, UTS, TE, hardness) to applied aging treatments

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements for every material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical property screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 4 wt.% Al sample, YS ~350–450 MPa band, tensile strength ~460–600 MPa, elongation ~8–55%; the 4Al alloy is only weakly affected by aging.

characterization_methods.purpose: hardness screening as a function of composition and aging treatment
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al (covering the 4Al sample).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.technique: metallographic analysis (grinding/polishing with standard metallographic techniques)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure investigation and checking for cracks, pores, or macrosegregations
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size.

unmapped_findings: Alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al (4 wt.% Al addition) is an intermediate variant of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP set; the 4 wt.% Al addition is explicitly reported among the intermediate variants. [b0019, b0024, b0025]
For Al content below 5 wt.%, a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature; this 4 wt.% Al sample therefore belongs to the single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel class. [b0015, b0031]

Compositions with 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al show the TWIP effect as the prevailing deformation mechanism (dislocation-based strain hardening followed by mechanical twinning at higher loads). [b0031]

Alloys with 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% Al additions are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening). [b0024]
Intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al show a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior than the ~8 wt.% Al variant. [b0025]

Al promotes the formation of nanoprecipitates upon aging with L'12 (L′1₂) structure and approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)3AlC (referred to as κ-carbides); these have a lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to an austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix (this is a general statement, not specifically quantified for the 450 °C/1 h condition). [b0015]

This sample was synthesized within the rapid alloy prototyping (RAP) combinatorial approach for trend screening and alloy maturation of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density TWIP and κ-carbide hardened steels. [b0019]
